statements.claim: Krishna reappeared among the gopis smiling, his face bright and open as a lotus.
statements.evidence: Bhav. Purana 10.32.1: 'tāsām āvirabhūc chauriḥ smayamāna-mukhāmbujaḥ' (Krishna appeared with a smiling lotus-face).

statements.claim: The gopis rose at once as if their very life had returned; their grief of separation was dispelled.
statements.evidence: 10.32.2, 8-9 and pack excerpt: 'they all rose at once as if their very life had returned... grief of separation was dispelled.'

statements.claim: Each gopi received him in her own way: one held his hand in folded palms, one took the betel he had been chewing, one knit her brows in loving anger, one gazed unblinking, one held him in her heart with closed eyes.
statements.evidence: 10.32.3-7: 'kācit karāmbujaṃ... jagṛhe 'ñjalinā mudā'; 'kācid añjalināgṛhṇāt tanvī tāmbūla-carvitam'; 'ekā bhru-kuṭim ābadhya prema-saṃrambha-vihvalā'; 'aparānimiṣad-dṛgbhyāṃ juṣāṇā'; 'taṃ kācin netra-randhreṇa hṛdi kṛtvā nimīlya.'

statements.claim: Krishna led them to the bright sandbank of the Yamuna; it was autumn with a full moon whose light dispelled darkness.
statements.evidence: 10.32.10-11: 'tāḥ samādāya kālindyā nirviśya pulinaṃ... śarac-candrāṃśu-sandoha-dhvasta-doṣā-tamaḥ.'

statements.claim: Their longings came to rest the way the ancient scriptures come to rest at their end.
statements.evidence: 10.32.12: 'manorathāntaṃ śrutayo yathā yayuḥ' (their desires ended as the śrutis do).

statements.claim: He sat on the seat the gopis had prepared for him in their own hearts, he the master of every master of yoga.
statements.evidence: 10.32.13: 'tatropaviṣṭo bhagavān sa īśvaro yogeśvarāntar-hṛdi kalpitāsanaḥ.'

statements.claim: They welcomed him with smiles, sidelong glances and the play of their brows.
statements.evidence: 10.32.14: 'sahāsa-līlekṣaṇa-vibhrama-bhruvā.'

statements.claim: Krishna had vanished twice before, and the gopis had searched the forest in endless grief.
statements.evidence: Not stated in 10.32.1-14 itself, but consistent with the corpus chain (previous story DKS_0104 'The Favored Gopi's Pride and Krishna's Second Vanishing').

statements.claim: Krishna did not explain his vanishing, and the gopis did not ask.
statements.evidence: True of the passage 10.32.1-14, which moves straight to the reunion and the return to the Yamuna sandbank.

notes: All named gestures, the setting and the moonlit sandbank map directly to 10.32.1-14. The 'vanished twice' is chain-referencing connective narration, consistent with DKS_0104.

statements.claim: On the moonlit Yamuna sandbank the gopis asked Krishna why he loves those who love him and yet seems to hold back.
statements.evidence: 10.32.15-16 ('śrī-gopya ūcuḥ') and pack summary: 'When the gopis asked why he loves those who love him, Krishna explained the ways of love.'

statements.claim: Some people serve those who do not serve them back, like compassionate parents serving a child.
statements.evidence: 10.32.17: 'bhajanty abhajato ye vai karuṇāḥ pitarau yathā.'

statements.claim: Others, even when served, do not serve in return; nothing can be expected from them.
statements.evidence: 10.32.18: 'bhajato 'pi na vai kecid bhajanty abhajataḥ kutaḥ.'

statements.claim: Krishna said he is like neither: he does not repay service like a trader settling accounts, but acts to deepen the love of those who serve him.
statements.evidence: 10.32.19: 'nāhaṃ tu sakhyo bhajato 'pi jantūn bhajāmy amīṣām anuvṛtti-vṛttaye.'

statements.claim: The gopis had cast aside the world and even the scriptures' obligations for his sake.
statements.evidence: 10.32.20: 'evaṃ mad-arthojjhita-loka-veda svānām hi vo mayy anuvṛttaye.'

statements.claim: Krishna said he could not repay them even with the lifespan of the gods.
statements.evidence: 10.32.21: 'na pāraye 'haṃ niravadya-saṃyujāṃ sva-sādhu-kṛtyaṃ vibudhāyuṣāpi vaḥ.'

statements.claim: Their goodness returned to them of itself; the love they gave was already its own reward.
statements.evidence: Pack summary: 'their love for him... could never be repaid, but that it returned to them of itself.'

statements.claim: He did not answer with a doctrine but with the way love behaves.
statements.evidence: Framing of the teaching in 10.32.17-21; matches the passage's form (a description of how love acts).

notes: Teaching claims track 10.32.15-21 closely, including the parent/child simile and the 'lifespan of the gods' line. No unsupported or contradicted statements.

statements.claim: A stranger came into Vrindavan wearing Achyuta's dress and ornaments, so that the gopis asked 'Who is this of wondrous beauty?'
statements.evidence: 10.47.1: 'ko 'yam apīvya-darśanaḥ... acyuta-veṣa-bhūṣaṇaḥ' and 'su-vismitāḥ... parivavrur utsukāḥ.'

statements.claim: The gopis received him with humility, shy smiles, sidelong glances and gentle words before he spoke.
statements.evidence: 10.47.2: 'taṃ praśrayeṇāvanatāḥ su-sat-kṛtaṃ sa-vrīḍa-hāsekṣaṇa-sūnṛtādibhiḥ.'

statements.claim: They recognized him as the attendant of the lord of the Yadavas, sent out of love; otherwise nothing in the cowherd settlement would be worth his remembering.
statements.evidence: 10.47.3-4: 'jānīmas tvāṃ yadu-pateḥ pārṣadaṃ samupāgatam / anyathā go-vraje tasya smaraṇīyaṃ na cakṣmahe.' Pack excerpt: 'sent by Krishna for love of his parents.'

statements.claim: The world's friendships are purposeful: a courtesan abandons a penniless man, subjects abandon a helpless king, birds forsake a fruitless tree, guests leave a house once the meal is done.
statements.evidence: 10.47.5-7: 'niḥsvaṃ tyajanti gaṇikā akalpaṃ nṛpatiṃ prajāḥ / khagā vīta-phalaṃ vṛkṣaṃ bhuktvā cātithayo gṛham.'

statements.claim: The gopis alone did not let go: with speech, body and mind fixed on Govinda, they sang his deeds and wept with all shame gone.
statements.evidence: 10.47.8-9: 'gopyo hi govinde gata-vāk-kāya-mānasāḥ / gāyantyaḥ prīya-karmāṇi rudantyaś ca gata-hriyaḥ.'

statements.claim: For months they had lived in the stillness of his absence.
statements.evidence: No duration is given in 10.47.1-9; 'months' is vague connective framing, consistent with the wider timeline (10.47.53: Uddhava later stays 'katicin māsān').

statements.claim: The settlement had been quiet since Krishna left, the flute silent.
statements.evidence: Atmosphere; matches the mood of separation in 10.47.1-9.

notes: All substantive claims (identity of the stranger, the greeting, the world's purposive friendships, the gopis' unbroken love) map to 10.47.1-9. The 'for months' duration is unsourced but vague, non-specific connective framing.

statements.claim: A gopi meditating on union with Krishna saw a honeybee settle near her and addressed it as a messenger.
statements.evidence: 10.47.10: 'kācin madhukaraṃ dṛṣṭvā dhyāyantī kṛṣṇa-saṅgamam.'

statements.claim: 'O bee, friend of the cheat, do not touch my feet' — she took it for a courier marked with the saffron of garlands crushed on other women's breasts, sent to mock her before the Yadu assembly.
statements.evidence: 10.47.11: 'madhupa kitava-bandho mā spṛśaṅghriṃ sapatnyāḥ... kuca-vilulita-mālā-kuṅkuma-śmaśrubhir naḥ... yadu-sadasi viḍambyaṃ yasya dūtas tvam īdṛk.'

statements.claim: He made them drink once the nectar of his lips and then abandoned them like cast-off flowers; she tells him to carry his favor to the proud women who now have him.
statements.evidence: 10.47.11-12: 'sakṛd adhara-sudhāṃ svāṃ mohinīṃ pāyayitvā... sumanasa iva sadyas tatyaje 'smān' and 'vahatu madhu-patis tan-māninīnāṃ prasādaṃ.'

statements.claim: She asks how the goddess of fortune serves his lotus feet though her heart too was stolen by his praises.
statements.evidence: 10.47.12: 'paricarati kathaṃ tat-pāda-padmaṃ nu padmā... hṛta-cetā... uttamaḥ-śloka-jalpaiḥ.'

statements.claim: She says enough of friendship with the dark one, though his stories can never be let go.
statements.evidence: 10.47.16: 'tad alam asita-sakhyair dustyajas tat-kathārthaḥ.'

statements.claim: Others who tasted a single drop of the nectar of his deeds abandoned home and family and wander like birds.
statements.evidence: 10.47.17: 'yad-anucarita-līlā-karṇa-pīyūṣa-vipruṭ-... gṛha-kuṭumbaṃ dīnam utsṛjya dīnā bahava iha vihaṅgā bhikṣu-caryāṃ caranti.'

statements.claim: We trusted him as a deer trusts a hunter's call and have felt the sharp hurt of longing again and again.
statements.evidence: 10.47.18: 'vayam ṛtam iva jihma-vyāhṛtaṃ śraddadhānāḥ kulika-rutam ivājñāḥ kṛṣṇa-vadhvo hariṇyaḥ... tan-nakha-sparśa-tīvra smara-ruja.'

statements.claim: If the bee is truly sent by her beloved it is to be honored and may choose what it wants, but how can it carry them back to one whose side none can leave and on whose chest Sri sits as bride?
statements.evidence: 10.47.19: 'priya-sakha punar āgāḥ preyasā preṣitaḥ kiṃ varaya... mānanīyo 'si me 'ṅga / nayasi katham ihāsmān dustyaja-dvandva-pārśvaṃ satatam urasi saumya śrīr vadhūḥ sākam āste.'

statements.claim: She asks whether he still dwells in the city of Madhu, remembers his father's house, kinsmen and the cowherds, ever speaks of his maidservants, and when he will place his aloe-fragrant arm on her head.
statements.evidence: 10.47.20: 'api bata madhu-puryām ārya-putro 'dhunāste $ smarati sa pitṛ-gehān saumya bandhūṃś ca gopān... kiṅkarīṇāṃ gṛṇīte % bhujam aguru-sugandhaṃ mūrdhny adhāsyat kadā nu.'

statements.claim: The gopi did not expect the bee to answer; the question was for the absent Krishna.
statements.evidence: Narrative inference from the monologue form of 10.47.10-20; no sourceable fact asserted.

notes: The lament maps verse-by-verse to 10.47.10-20 (Bhramara-gita); all reproaches, similes and closing questions are supported.

statements.claim: Uddhava came from Krishna bearing a message from his own mouth, sent for this purpose.
statements.evidence: 10.47.27: 'śrūyatāṃ priya-sandeśo bhavatīnāṃ sukhāvahaḥ' (hear the dear message bringing you happiness).

statements.claim: Before the message, Uddhava praised the gopis: through gifts, vows, austerities, sacrifice, japa, study and self-control they had offered sons, husbands, bodies, kinsmen and homes to a single love and become peerless.
statements.evidence: 10.47.23-26: 'dāna-vrata-tapo-homa japa-svādhyāya-saṃyamaiḥ... diṣṭyā putrān patīn dehān sva-janān bhavanāni ca... anuttamā.'

statements.claim: Krishna's message: he pervades all beings as the elements do; he creates, preserves and destroys by himself, being pure knowledge untouched by the gunas; fix your mind wholly on him and you will soon attain him.
statements.evidence: 10.47.29-35 and pack excerpt: 'My separation from you is never complete, as ether, air, fire, water and earth pervade all beings... fix your mind wholly on me and you will soon attain me.'

statements.claim: This was the whole conclusion of the scriptures, of yoga and of the wise.
statements.evidence: 10.47.32: 'etad-antaḥ samāmnāyo yogaḥ sāṅkhyaṃ manīṣiṇām.'

statements.claim: He reminded them it was he who had played with them at night in the forest of Vraja.
statements.evidence: 10.47.36: 'yā mayā krīḍatā rātryāṃ vane 'smin vraja āsthitāḥ.'

statements.claim: The gopis answered that Govinda could not forget the moonlit nights in Vrindavan, the groves white with kumuda and kunda, the rasa dance with ankle-bells ringing.
statements.evidence: 10.47.42: 'vṛndāvane kumuda-kunda-śaśāṅka-ramye reme kvaṇac-caraṇa-nūpura-rāsa-goṣṭhyām.'

statements.claim: Will the Dasarha come back, scorched by a sorrow of his own making? He has won a kingdom and slain his enemies; what are we forest-dwellers to that great soul?
statements.evidence: 10.47.43-45: 'apy eṣyatīha dāśārhas taptāḥ sva-kṛtayā śucā / kasmāt kṛṣṇa ihāyāti prāpta-rājyo hatāhitaḥ / kim asmābhir vanaukobhir anyābhir vā mahātmanaḥ.'

statements.claim: Who could bear to give up the memory of him? The rivers, hills, forest paths, cows and the flute's sound call back the son of Nanda again and again.
statements.evidence: 10.47.47-49: 'ka utsaheta santyaktum uttamaḥśloka-saṃvidam / saric-chaila-vanoddeśā gāvo veṇu-ravā ime / punaḥ punaḥ smārayanti nanda-gopa-sutaṃ bata.'

statements.claim: 'O lord, O lord of Rama, O lord of Vraja, remover of sorrows.'
statements.evidence: 10.47.51 reads 'he nātha he ramā-nātha vraja-nāthārti-nāśana' — 'ramā-nātha' is lord of Ramā (Lakshmi); the story's 'lord of Rama' (no diacritics) is a transliteration nuance, not a different claim.

statements.claim: Uddhava was Krishna's friend and counsellor, a man of learning and restraint.
statements.evidence: Characterization consistent with the passage (he delivers Krishna's private, theologically dense message and later consoles the gopis), though not literally stated in 10.47.21-51.

statements.claim: For months the women of Vrindavan had grieved; they had even pleaded with a bee, mistaking it for a courier.
statements.evidence: The bee episode is the immediately preceding story (DKS_0109, 10.47.10-20), linked in the corpus chain; 'for months' is connective duration framing.

notes: Message and reply both track 10.47.21-51. Minor note: 'O lord of Rama' renders 'ramā-nātha' (lord of Lakshmi) without diacritics — ambiguous transliteration, not a substantive error.

statements.claim: Uddhava stayed some months in Vrindavan, dispelling the gopis' sorrow.
statements.evidence: 10.47.53: 'uvāsa katicin māsān gopīnāṃ vinudan śucaḥ.'

statements.claim: Day by day he walked the country, seeing the rivers, forests, mountain valleys and flowering trees, and the gopis' minds agitated with absorption in Krishna.
statements.evidence: 10.47.55-56: 'sarid-vana-giri-droṇīr vīkṣan kusumitān drumān / ... gopīnāṃ kṛṣṇāveśātma-viklavam.'

statements.claim: He declared the cowherd women have reached the highest place: their hearts are fixed on Govinda, the soul of all; what use are brahmana births against the taste of his endless stories?
statements.evidence: 10.47.57: 'etāḥ paraṃ tanu-bhṛto bhuvi gopa-vadhvo govinda eva nikhilātmani rūḍha-bhāvāḥ... kiṃ brahma-janmabhir ananta-kathā-rasasya.'

statements.claim: Where are these forest women and where is the supreme self — yet the Lord grants his highest good even to the ignorant who serve him, like a king of medicines.
statements.evidence: 10.47.58: 'kvemāḥ striyo vana-carīr... kṛṣṇe kva caiṣa paramātmani... nanv īśvaro 'nubhajato 'viduṣo 'pi sākṣāc chreyas tanoty agada-rāja ivopayuktaḥ.'

statements.claim: The favor of being held in Krishna's arms at the rasa festival was given to the Vraja women, a blessing not granted even to Sri or the lotus-fragrant heavenly women.
statements.evidence: 10.47.59: 'nāyaṃ śriyo 'ṅga u nitānta-rateḥ prasādaḥ svar-yoṣitāṃ nalina-gandha-rucāṃ kuto 'nyāḥ / rāsotsave 'sya bhuja-daṇḍa-gṛhīta-kaṇṭha-labdhāśiṣāṃ ya udagād vraja-vallabhīnām.'

statements.claim: These women threw away their families and the path of the Āryas for the path the scriptures search out.
statements.evidence: 10.47.60: 'yā dustyajaṃ sva-janam ārya-pathaṃ ca hitvā bhejur mukunda-padavīṃ śrutibhir vimṛgyām.'

statements.claim: He wished: 'May I become any shrub, creeper or herb in Vrindavan, blessed by the dust of these gopis' feet,' bowing to that foot-dust again and again.
statements.evidence: 10.47.60-62: 'āsām aho caraṇa-reṇu-juṣām ahaṃ syāṃ vṛndāvane kim api gulma-latauṣadhīnām' and 'vande nanda-vraja-strīṇāṃ pāda-reṇum abhīkṣṇaśaḥ.'

statements.claim: He comforted Nanda, Yashoda and the cowherds, and they honored him, their wish that their minds rest at Krishna's lotus feet wherever their karma wanders them.
statements.evidence: 10.47.63-66: 'taṃ nirgataṃ samāsādya nānopāyana-pāṇayaḥ / manaso vṛttayo naḥ syuḥ kṛṣṇa pādāmbujāśrayāḥ / karmabhir bhrāmyamāṇānāṃ yatra kvāpīśvarecchayā.'

statements.claim: Bowing to Krishna he told him of the abundance of the Vraja-dwellers' devotion.
statements.evidence: 10.47.68: 'kṛṣṇāya praṇipatyāha bhakty-udrekaṃ vrajaukasām.'

statements.claim: They honored him as they would a brother.
statements.evidence: 10.47.67 says they honored him with Krishna-bhakti ('sabhājito gopaiḥ kṛṣṇa-bhaktyā'); the 'brother' warmth is connective hospitality framing, not contradicted.

notes: Uddhava's praise, the shrub-wish, the farewell and the return to Mathura all map directly to 10.47.52-68.

statements.claim: Akrura had been sent by Kamsa, king of Mathura, to fetch Krishna and Balarama to the city.
statements.evidence: 10.38.6: 'kaṃso batādyākṛta me 'ty-anugrahaṃ... prahito 'munā hareḥ' (Kamsa showed grace by sending me [to see] Hari); the errand is the episode's premise, confirmed by the corpus chain (DKS_0114 'Akrura Reveals Kamsa's Plan').

statements.claim: On the road he wondered what merit or austerity had earned him the rare sight of Krishna.
statements.evidence: 10.38.2-3: 'kiṃ mayācaritaṃ bhadraṃ kiṃ taptaṃ paramaṃ tapaḥ / mamaitad durlabhaṃ manya uttamaḥ-śloka-darśanam.'

statements.claim: Even Kamsa had unwittingly shown him grace by sending him.
statements.evidence: 10.38.6: 'kaṃso batādyākṛta me 'ty-anugrahaṃ drakṣye 'ṅghri-padmaṃ prahito 'munā hareḥ.'

statements.claim: Krishna's feet are worshipped by Brahma, Shiva, the goddess of fortune, the sages and the Satvatas; they wandered the forest herding cows, marked with the gopis' saffron.
statements.evidence: 10.38.7: 'yad arcitaṃ brahma-bhavādibhiḥ suraiḥ śriyā ca devyā munibhiḥ sa-sātvataiḥ... go-cāraṇāyānucaraiś carad vane yad gopikānāṃ kuca-kuṅkumāṅkitam.'

statements.claim: Those feet give shelter to men fleeing the serpent of time, and at them Indra and Bali placed offerings and won the lordship of the three worlds.
statements.evidence: 10.38.15-16: 'dattābhayaṃ kāla-bhujāṅga-raṃhasā prodvejitānāṃ śaraṇaiṣiṇāṃ nṛṇām / samarhaṇaṃ yatra nidhāya kauśikas tathā baliś cāpa jagat-trayendratām.'

statements.claim: He imagined the face — fine cheeks and nose, smiling glance, eyes like red lotuses — of the Lord who descended of his own will into the Yadu line to lift the earth's burden.
statements.evidence: 10.38.8-9, 12: 'su-kapola-nāsikaṃ smitāvalokāruṇa-kañja-locanam... bhārāvatārāya bhuvo nijecchayā... sa cāvatīrṇaḥ kila satvatānvaye.'

statements.claim: He pictured Krishna's lotus hand on his head, the embrace of his two great arms, and the voice saying 'O Akrura,' which would make his birth fulfilled.
statements.evidence: 10.38.14-15, 19-20: 'patitasya me vibhuḥ śirasy adhāsyan nija-hasta-paṅkajam... dorbhyāṃ bṛhadbhyāṃ parirapsyate 'tha mām... māṃ vakṣyate 'krūra tatety uruśravāḥ.'

statements.claim: He feared Krishna, who sees within and without, might read the errand and turn away — but Krishna holds no favorite and no enemy.
statements.evidence: 10.38.17, 21: 'na mayy upaiṣyaty ari-buddhim acyutaḥ... viśva-dṛk... antarbahiś cetasa etad īhitaṃ kṣetra-jña īkṣaty amalena cakṣuṣā' and 'na tasya kaścid dayitaḥ suhṛttamo na cāpriyo dveṣya upekṣya eva vā.'

statements.claim: He dared to hope Balarama would embrace him too.
statements.evidence: 10.38.22: 'kiṃ cāgrajo māvanataṃ yadūttamaḥ smayan pariṣvajya gṛhītam añjalau.'

statements.claim: At Gokula as the day ended he came down from the chariot and saw the Lord's footprints marked with the lotus and other signs.
statements.evidence: 10.38.14 ('athāvarūḍhaḥ sapadīśayo rathāt') and pack excerpt: 'he arrived at Gokula at sunset, gazing at the footprints of the Lord marked with the lotus and other signs.'

statements.claim: The feet whose dust adorns the crowns of all the protectors of the worlds.
statements.evidence: 10.38.24 (same chapter, next story's pack): 'padāni tasyākhila-loka-pāla-kirīṭa-juṣṭāmala-pāda-reṇoḥ.'

notes: Akrura's interior monologue maps verse-by-verse to 10.38.1-23; the foot-dust/crowns image is 10.38.24, the same chapter immediately following.

statements.claim: Akrura reached Vraja at evening — weak sun, tawny moon in the crimson sky, birds in their nests, cows home lowing with calves bound, milkmen calling the kine by name and kindling fires.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.80 (in pack): 'the sun, with weakened rays, set... the disc of the moon became tawny coloured, when the birds entered into their nests... the cows came back, and having their calves bound (to stakes)... the milk-men... began to call their kine by names... fire was set to dried cow-dung by Gopas.'

statements.claim: At the milking-place among the calves he saw two youths — one dark, one fair, big-armed and garlanded, feet marked with the flag, thunderbolt, goad and lotus.
statements.evidence: 10.38.27-30: 'dadarśa kṛṣṇaṃ rāmaṃ ca vraje go-dohanaṃ gatau / kiśorau śyāmala-śvetau śrī-niketau bṛhad-bhujau / dhvaja-vajrāṅkuśāmbhojaiś cihnitair aṅghribhir vrajam... sragviṇau vana-mālinau.' Harivamsha: 'he saw Krishna stationed at the milking-place in the midst of calves.'

statements.claim: Krishna was dark as the leaf of a full-blown lotus; Balarama white as jasmine.
statements.evidence: Vishnu Purana 5.17 (in pack): 'he saw Krishńa amongst the cattle, dark as the leaf of the full blown lotus... Akrúra also beheld there Balabhadra, white as a jasmine, a swan, or the moon.'

statements.claim: They stood at the meeting point of boyhood and youth, their radiance scattering the evening's gloom.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.80: 'at the junction of boyhood and youth'; 10.38.32: 'diśo vitimirā rājan kurvāṇau prabhayā svayā.'

statements.claim: Akrura's face opened with delight.
statements.evidence: Vishnu Purana 5.17: 'his countenance expanded with delight.'

statements.claim: He jumped from the chariot, overwhelmed with love, hair standing on end, eyes brimming, and threw himself into the dust of the Lord's feet, crying out over the foot-dust that crowns the heads of all world-protectors.
statements.evidence: 10.38.24-25, 33-34: 'rathād avaskandya sa teṣv aceṣṭata prabhor amūny aṅghri-rajāṃsy aho iti' and 'premṇordhva-romāśru-kalākulekṣaṇaḥ... rathāt tūrṇam avaplutya so 'krūraḥ sneha-vihvalaḥ / bhagavad-darśanāhlāda-bāṣpa-paryākulekṣaṇaḥ.'

statements.claim: This, he knew, was the highest achievement of embodied beings — to lie in that dust, free of pretence, fear and grief.
statements.evidence: 10.38.26: 'dehaṃ-bhṛtām iyān artho hitvā dambhaṃ bhiyaṃ śucam.'

statements.claim: He praised the Lord who once lay on a fig-leaf at the dissolution of all things and once stepped over the three worlds as a dwarf.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.80: 'who lay on a fig-leaf at the time of the universal dissolution, and who assumed the form of a dwarf at the time of imposing on Bali.'

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama came forward, lifted him up, embraced him, asked his welfare, gave him a seat of honor and offered a cow to the guest; Balarama washed his tired feet.
statements.evidence: 10.38.35-39: 'bhagavāṃs tam abhipretya... saṅkarṣaṇaś ca praṇatam upaguhya... pṛṣṭvātha sv-āgataṃ tasmai nivedya ca varāsanam / nivedya gāṃ cātithaye saṃvāhya śrāntam... rāmaḥ parama-dharma-vit' (saṃvāhya śrāntam = bathing the weary guest; the foot-washing courtesy is Rama's part in 10.38.39).

statements.claim: Nanda, the cowherd chief, asked how the Yadavas fared under the cruel king who killed his sister's children while she wept.
statements.evidence: 10.38.40-41: 'papraccha sat-kṛtaṃ nandaḥ kathaṃ stha niranugrahe / yo 'vadhīt sva-svasus tokān krośantyā asu-tṛp khalaḥ.'

statements.claim: No one demanded his business or asked what message he carried.
statements.evidence: 10.38.42: 'itthaṃ sūnṛtayā vācā nandena su-sabhājitaḥ' (honored by Nanda with gentle words); the rest is narrative inference from the reception.

notes: Evening setting from Harivamsha 1.80, lotus/jasmine comparisons from Vishnu Purana 5.17, and the reception from 10.38.23-42 — all three pack sources used; tradition_note corroborates.
